title: FOOTBALL | Head Coach Jeff Lebby Press Conference - 11/27/26
text: All right, guys. Thanks for being here tonight. Coach is going to start with an updated statement whenever he's ready and then we'll get started with questions after that. Please raise your hand and ask a question. Go ahead, coach. >> Yeah, for us today, I did I was really excited with how we started, how we played, our effort, our physicality. [snorts] I hate how the game ended. U really disappointing how we came out defensively in the second half with the third downs and them being able to convert and keeping drives alive. That to me was the difference in the game at that moment and then we get back in it. Three-point game, first and 10 at the plus 41. Kid makes an incredible playh for them and and that was frustrating because we weren't able to overcome it at that point. So, I was I thought our guys were ready to go play, fought their butt off, really disappointed in in how it ended. For our guys, just like we just talked about in there, it's been a tale of two seasons. and the way we started the year, the excitement, the energy, everything that went into it as we were 4-0, the number 16 team in the country, things happened in this game. Uh, man, and it's like I tell them all the time, this game will bring you to your knees. And so, being able to respond the right way, uh, and understand what's next and what's next for us, the immediiacy of retention, our 27 roster, the urgency that we're going to operate with inside our walls every single day to put something on the field, man, that Mississippi State is going to be incredibly proud of. And uh that's going to get ready to happen. It starts right now. I've already talked to a couple of guys in that locker room. Our urgency, how we do what we do in this off season will give us the ability to do something incredibly special. So there is there's incredible belief by every single one of those guys in that room. I think you saw that today. Proud of that. Um with that, I'll open it up. So I'll Robbie first and Steve. >> Yeah, coach, you talked about it a little bit. The interception there [clears throat] and it's a three-point game. They go down and score and you're driving. you have a chance to kind of keep maintaining right there. Did you feel like that was kind of a back breaker for your guys the way that happened? >> It it it absolutely was. Again, we're first and 10 plus 41. We're down three points in the fourth quarter and we've got exactly what we want. We're going to pitch and catch to the four and kid makes an incredible play and uh and he does. And then again, now the game goes to 10 points. Then we go three and out. We have the false start on second down. We don't convert on the third down. We got Frisco. The coverage dictated that's where the ball needed to go. So, really good decision by Bill. Would have loved to seen us throwing catch in that situation. Could have created a huge chunk and and again got us right back in it to cut it to three, but again, we weren't able to overcome it. >> Coach, you know what it's like to have the Eggbo and trophy in your possession, but we haven't had it here at Mississippi State since 2022. And this is a game that means so much to a lot of people. What what needs to be done? Do there need to be more emphasis placed on this game or what would you suggest needs to happen to win this game next year? >> No, for for us it's it's about playing all four quarters and we're in the middle of fighting to go win the game like like we just talked about first and 10 plus 41. It's a three-point game. Having the opportunity to go take control of the game and we don't do it in that moment. Their guy made an incredible play. Credit to him. But for us, it's about being able to make our plays throughout the game to to have real game control and uh and to be able to find a way to go win. So, there's been incredible emphasis on this game. It means a ton to me. It means a ton to our football uh team and our program. Disappointed and and not good enough and hate it for our fans. Hate it for the people that love Mississippi State. And again, for us, disappointing, upsetting. I am dang proud of how our guys try to come out and fight their butt off to go win and I think that was evident. >> James, what do you feel like were some of the biggest problems you guys had on third down? >> Yeah, we didn't throw and catch real well on third down. Uh we had the ability to create some chunks. We had Fris a couple of times and again the coverage dictated that the ball be pushed down the field because how they were playing underneath. I I would have loved to seen us connect on a couple of those things. I mentioned it, but defensively, you know, not being able to get off the field on third downs. Those first two drives of the second half, that was the difference. As they come out and score two touchdowns on their first two drives, we weren't able to make those plays. And for us, I thought we played really fast protectionally. I thought we were really good up until the end of the game and did some really good things, but again, we weren't able to make enough plays and and they did. Carlin, >> coach, I'm not sure of the exact score, but I believe it was a one-point game. You got that fourth and four in the fourth quarter and you decided to punt. What went into that decision about there was I thought there was still enough time. We had played good defense. They had gotten their touchdown because of the interception being down at the 1 inch line. And so I felt like we were in a position to be able to go get a stop because we had gotten the stops in the two prior drives after the first two drives getting back on the field in the third quarter. It didn't work out that way. Um, but that that was my thought process. >> Colin, saw Fluff kind of giving it his all today. I know he's coming back next year, but what did you see from him going into the game and then what did you see from him on the field? >> Yeah, he really determined and I think you saw that today. A guy that played incredibly tough, did some great things, made a great play on second 12 down there. Uh, made it made a great catch, really good play by Billy. And then he did he ran incredibly tough. was exactly what we wanted and needed him to be to give us a chance. >> Sam, >> have you been informed at all that you'll be the head coach here for next season? >> That hadn't been a conversation. Um, I have been continued to focus on this football team, finding a way to give us an opportunity to go win. I fully intend on being a head football coach here until somebody tells me I'm not. But again, I think we all understand like frustrating, disappointing, not good enough. Um, our guys believe and believe in a great way. And I think as we continue to build this roster for the 27 season, we're we're going to have the ability to do something incredibly special. And I'm going to continue to point forward on that. Steve, >> along those lines, looking to next year, I mean, you know, Kamario has come out, said he wants to play for you in 2027. If you were trying to sell your football program and your vision for next year, how do you sell tickets? What do you kind of share with the recruits and with the fans and why they should support Mississippi State? >> Yeah, I I do. I think you go back to the beginning of the season and it has it's been a tale of two seasons. That's exactly what I opened with and there's been some frustrating moments, a ton of them here as of late and it hadn't been good enough and disappointing for everybody involved. Nobody more than myself. But when you look up, we're 4-0. We go on the road and beat Minnesota the way we do. We go to South Carolina and beat them the way we do. And come home and beat Missouri, we're 4-0. We're the number 16 team in the country. That did happen. Those are real things. And in those moments, we were a pretty healthy football team. I'm not ever going to use it as as an excuse. I hadn't talked about it one time and won't. We've got to be better. We weren't good enough. But we were 4-0. We were the number 16 team in the country. And that is a real thing. And so I think people understand that. You got a glimpse of what we've got at quarterback. We got the best football player in the country. I'm not going to shy away from that. We do. who believes in me, who believes in our football team, who believes in our program, our university, and we're going to get ready to go fight our ass off and put a great product on the field for everybody involved. And that's uh that's going to happen. >> Jake, before the season kicked off, you said the offensive line can get a lot better. Struggle again this year, struggle again today. Just for that unit specifically, what do you have to do this offseason to make sure this doesn't happen again next year? >> Player acquisition. We've got to do a great job taking the right ones. That will be critical. We got to retain the right ones and then we we're going to be incredibly aggressive on how we do what we do in this portal cycle uh to be able to put man incredible pieces around one [snorts] and I've continued to talk about that building this program around a young man that is as elite as he is. So that's how we fix it and then from a staffing standpoint obviously in the middle of going through some things and hopefully that's nailed down here the next four or five days. talked about the retention piece and bringing back some key players. But as far as that acquisition side of things, what are you looking for to to help build this roster next season? What's the biggest points of emphasis outside the offensive line? >> Offensive line obviously is as we mentioned and then when you look at the defensive side of the football, uh we do we've got to do a great job in the secondary. We got to do a great job at safety and then replacing some of these guys in the front. You know, you lose guys like Jer and Will who had an unbelievable amount of production. Jason Jenkins, another one that was a a great role player for us. So, we're going to [snorts] have to address all three levels. Um, but at the end of the day, man, it is it's about the front on both sides of the football and then making sure we've got the pieces we need from a secondary standpoint. >> Elijah, >> coach, uh, Miss converted five third downs to start the second half. What adjustments did they make in the second half and what was making your guys struggle? >> They [clears throat] did. We we got caught in a couple of man calls where we were playing a little too soft and they did a really good job of pitching and catching and then they caught us in a couple of zone calls where we didn't take enough air out of it with with our coverage. And so one of the first things I mentioned that was probably the most frustrating thing is how they converted on those third downs and the first two drives in the second half. That really did it it changed the game and then [snorts] we got momentum back and then obviously the interception happens. David, >> related to the retention, the flip side of that is creating room on the roster. Have those conversations been taking place too with guys who may not be here next year? >> That'll all all of that will start this next week. >> Carlo, >> coach, uh, Billy Pucket kind of thrusted into the position of the starting quarterback for the last eight games of the year or so. Um, to finish the way he did the last two games of the season, what can you say about his toughness and commitment to the university and the team? I I've continued to talk about Bill and how much he loves Mississippi State. How much he loves this football team. The toughness showed up in an incredible way today. Did some great things for us. Gave us a chance. Hate that the the pick happens. But again, that guy makes an incredible play in that moment, but appreciative of Billy and who he's been. And he did. He got thrown into it. It is. It's three years in a row. Red shirt freshman quarterback today. In the last two years, true freshman quarterback in this game. that's happened. Hopeful to to look up a year from now and that's not the case and we got a true junior ready to step out there on the field and and start. >> Stephen, I know you correct me if I'm wrong, but I believe everybody with rare exceptions under contract on your staff for for next year. I mean, do you anticipate making any additional changes? I know some guys may come and go, but do you plan to make any additional changes? Yeah, I'm in the middle of looking at everything. I mentioned this, I think it was a couple of Mondays ago, not just from a football standpoint, football coaching standpoint, but everything programmatically to make sure we are doing everything we possibly can to [clears throat] take advantage of this special moment that we're going to have in 2027. And that is my focus. It's all layers. It's everybody inside our walls to make sure we're putting the right people inside our building uh to go be as good as we can possibly be. >> AB coach, I know last year we benefited from the AP audit as far as just five wins. Is there any been any indication that that might be in the card this year? >> That that has not. >> J, >> when we last talked after Tennessee Tech, you talked about how you're going to be who you're supposed to be and you have a lot of confidence in that. Um, what do you feel like you're supposed to be and what and where does the confidence come from? >> Yeah. Again, I'm I'm going to go back to how things started and it hadn't been good enough. I'm going to continue to say that, too. But the reality is is we were on pace to do something pretty special. Things happened. It hadn't been near good enough since then, but for me, I've got great confidence in in who I am and and where we're going. And K1 and I talked about it actually last night at the hotel. You get us two in a room and both of us understand where we're headed. And there's a lot of excitement, there's a lot of energy. It's going to continue to be that way. We've got to find ways to make sure we're putting all of the pieces around him that we can. and that's what we're going to do. But for me, there's not a lack of confidence in being able to go lead this program. That's for sure. Sam, >> just with the timing of Kamario announcing his decision to come back, I know the transfer port is not open yet, but have you seen that kind of help the team in terms of some of those retention conversations you're having and guys being excited knowing that he's coming back and maybe that changes their decisions as well. >> No, it's a huge deal. Great players like to play with great players. That's the reality of it. And talent, uh, it does. that attracts talent and so I think people across the country understand man there's going to be a light shining on Starkville next year and that that's a real thing and people want to be a part of that and so our conversations with guys on our roster right now are completely different even a year ago and so that momentum is building uh it's a real thing and we've got to continue to build on coach >> thanks coach >> appreciate it thank
